order_of_operations.step: Search the codebase to locate the files under review and their callers.
Read the contract files first, then the code, then the tests.
Read in batches. One pass for structure, one pass for detail.
Run evidence commands only when a finding needs proof.
Write nothing unless the user asks for a written report.

searching.rule: Start with a meaning-based search, then move to exact pattern search for a symbol.
Look for callers before judging a method. A method is only wrong relative to its callers.
Search for the tests of the file under review early. Tests state the intended behaviour.
Search for a second copy of the same rule. Duplication is the most common P2.
Stop searching once the finding is proven. More evidence does not change the severity.

reading.rule: Read the whole file before quoting a line from it. A line out of context produces wrong findings.
Read the caller of every method you plan to criticise.
Read the configuration that changes the behaviour you are judging.
Do not claim a defect in code you have not read. Say "not reviewed" instead.

evidence_commands.rule: Build and run targeted tests when the change builds. Report only output you saw.
Use a diff command to establish the review scope. Do not guess what changed.
Prefer a narrow test filter over the whole suite. Speed keeps the review honest.
Quote the failing assertion, not the whole log.
Never state that a command ran unless its output appeared.
If output is truncated or unclear, say so and lower the confidence.

forbidden_actions.rule: Never edit product source, tests, build files, or docs. This mode reports, it does not repair.
Never run a command that mutates the working tree: checkout, reset, clean, stash, format, or codegen.
Never install, restore, or upgrade a package to make a review easier.
Never disable an analyser, a warning, or a failing test to get a clean build for the review.
Never commit, push, tag, or open a pull request.
Never write a secret, token, or customer value into a report.

residual_risk.note: Command execution cannot be made read-only. The ban above is a rule, not a sandbox.
residual_risk.rule: Prefer the least powerful command that answers the question.
Say so if a command had a side effect, even an intended one.

writing_reports.rule: Write a report only when the user asks for a file, or when the review is too long for chat.
Put review reports under plans/ only. Never elsewhere.
Name the file for what it reviews, for example plans/refresh-path-review.md.
Use the report template from 7_communication.xml, unchanged.
Keep the chat message short when a file is written. State the path, the verdict, and the counts.

api_verification.rule: Prefer the compiler, the installed package metadata, and existing call sites over memory.
Prefer official documentation over blog posts or forum answers.
If a signature cannot be checked in this workspace, write "unknown" and name what would settle it.
Never invent a member, an overload, an attribute, an enum value, or a default.
Never describe behaviour you have not read or run.

delegation.rule: Fixes belong to code mode. State the finding and the sample, then hand off.
Design questions belong to architect mode.
A whole-repo one-shot audit belongs to the ponytail-audit skill, not to a long session here.
A debt register belongs to the tech-debt skill.
A safe mechanical refactor loop belongs to the refactor skill.
Say which one applies, in one line, instead of doing all of them here.
